name: Anlon Technology Solutions Limited
sector: Airport safety equipment assembly, OEM distribution and lifecycle services
identity_note: INE0LR101013, ANLON, active traded SM series. No subsidiary in reviewed FY26 CARO; standalone Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. This is not Anlon Healthcare. Main-board migration approved by shareholders but completion not established.
summary: Airport-equipment assembler and OEM lifecycle-services provider with genuine rapid revenue growth, but persistently weak cash realization and a demanding dated price. At ₹700, the funded conditional base yields4.1% annualized versus a 15% hurdle; GQS is capped at 5 by recurring cash conversion weakness. BQS 5.7 and IAS 3.375 place it in weak setup / value-trap risk, not a compounder. Fresh equity improves survival, not automatic per-share value.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Anlon assembles and supplies specialized airport safety/runway equipment and provides OEM-linked maintenance, spares and engineering services. The opportunity is genuine localization and an expanding installed service base; FY2026 assembly revenue rose from ₹6.46 crore to ₹53.41 crore. The decisive weakness is that several years of accounting profits have not converted into operating cash. The actual June equity raise improves funding resilience, but does not make every price attractive. At the dated ₹700 close, the financed base case yields 4.1% annualized against a 15% hurdle. BQS 5.7, GQS 5.0 after the cash-quality cap, and IAS 3.375 place this in weak setup / value-trap risk. It is an execution-dependent industrial growth thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. Better verified collections or a materially lower entry price would change the assessment. [S1][ALLOT][M1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Anlon Technology Solutions Limited; ANLON; ISIN INE0LR101013; NSE SME. Research cutoff 20 October 2026. The October 19 close was ₹700; 7,509,800 current issued shares imply equity capitalization ₹525.686 crore. The allotment filing and active SM security row agree. The company is not Anlon Healthcare. Scope is standalone: no subsidiary was identified in the reviewed FY2026 CARO. The accounts use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards (AS), not Ind AS. Five-year investor horizon to 19 October 2031, assumed nominal INR hurdle 15% before personal tax, and illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference, not a suggested allocation. [S1][ALLOT][M1]

G1 Integrity, G2 Reliability, G3 Funding and G4 Tradability are all Conditional. The audit is unmodified, but related-party commercial terms, OEM duration, cash deployment and execution must be monitored. Audited historical aggregates reconcile sufficiently for a conditional model; no unexplained critical reliability gap was found. Actual equity and cash facilities fund the modeled stresses without an assumed new rescue. Trading is observed, but lots and concentrated participation constrain implementation. These findings are not guarantees.

Confidence is Medium for governance, historical financials, organic growth decomposition, capital returns and valuation inputs. Annual figures are primary-verified; five-year growth is real, but not decomposed fully into units, mix and currency. Forecast uncertainty is wide and separate from confidence in retrieving the historical evidence. October cash is modeled from March plus actual financing, not presented as an observed bank balance.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5; MOAT 6; REV 8; DUR 6; CAP 5; CASH 3; BAL 7; EXEC 6; EARN 7; R 1; D 4; P 3; L 5. Each is used once in the prescribed formula and linked to evidence in the audit tab. BQS raw/final 5.70, full evidence coverage; GQS raw 6.50, final 5.00 because CASH 3 reflects recurring poor realization, not merely capex spending; IAS raw/final 3.375, full coverage. No governance or funding-failure numerical override is applied. IAS uses BQS exactly once: 0.25×5.70 + 0.35×1 + 0.20×4 + 0.10×3 + 0.10×5 = 3.375.

BQS weights are GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. GQS uses REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH 10%. Exact contribution arithmetic and the cash cap are retained in score_audit. A one-point change in MOAT moves BQS by 0.20 and IAS by 0.05; a one-point change in CAP moves them by 0.12 and 0.03. Neither changes the classification. A genuine sustained improvement from CASH 3 to4 would remove the persistent-cash cap and change GQS substantially; that requires new collection evidence, not an optimistic forecast.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business combines manufacturing/assembly of fire and runway equipment with engineering, spares, installation, training and maintenance. FY2026 audited segment revenue was ₹53.407 crore manufacturing/assembly and ₹52.5099 crore engineering. Segment EBIT was ₹8.0882 crore and ₹12.7751 crore respectively, before unallocated expense/income. Assembly margin was approximately 15.14%, below engineering 24.33%. Total revenue was ₹105.9169 crore, with goods ₹75.9549 crore and services ₹29.9620 crore. The call’s approximate 50% manufacturing, 27% AMC and 23% distribution split is management’s business description, not a replacement for the audited segment table. [S1][CALL]

Customers buy specialist safety equipment and service support, often through tenders and project acceptance. Billing, retention and unbilled work explain why orders and recognized profits are not equivalent to cash. March trade receivables plus unbilled revenue were ₹47.4004 crore. Acuité described approximately 80% aviation-sector concentration as of March 2026. The latest customer-level concentration is not disclosed in the material reviewed; the prospectus’s FY2022 top-five share of 39.33% and FY2021 58.15% are historical, not current estimates. [S1][RATING][P1]

Foreign-currency earnings were ₹8.0842 crore; export goods were nil in the note. The ₹4.3118 crore fees/know-how/professional line is foreign earnings, not additional royalty expense. Actual royalty expenditure was ₹0.9658 crore and imported components ₹26.4205 crore. These flows are already in the operating accounts; they are not added again as extra revenue or cost. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is specialist OEM access plus installed-equipment service capability: product qualification, technician familiarity, spares and response requirements can make replacement costly for customers. The evidence is actual service revenue, repeat orders and demonstrated assembly, not merely certifications. Durability depends on OEM renewals, customer qualification and satisfactory service. Failure can come from an OEM selling directly, appointing another partner, technology change or a capable competing integrator. [S1][PRES][CALL]

Issuer presentation claims include Rosenbauer exclusivity for Indian airports and other customers except AAI and defence, Bucher for Indian aviation, and other product-specific rights. These exceptions matter. Complete contracts and independent confirmation of every term were not obtained; the issuer agreements category was empty when checked. The claimed 90% airport presence concerns Rosenbauer equipment and is not a measured Anlon revenue market share. No unconditional monopoly is assumed. [PRES][SITE]

Economically useful comparators are Rosenbauer’s global OEM and Bucher Municipal, not automatic valuation peers. Rosenbauer FY2025 revenue was €1,429 million, EBIT €84.5 million, margin 5.9%, PAT €54.3 million and CFO €87.1 million. Bucher Municipal had CHF605.2 million sales and CHF57.0 million EBIT, about 9.42%. Their scale, owned technology, manufacturing intensity, currencies and accounting differ from Anlon’s distribution/service mix. Their lower margins warn against assuming localization must expand Anlon’s margin; their quoted multiples are not used. BEML’s August 2024 airfield-fire-tender technology EOI demonstrates a route for competing Indian capability, especially in AAI/defence. An EOI is not proof of a completed tie-up or an awarded order. [R1][R2][COMP]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue history, ₹ crore: FY2020 restated 13.6865; FY2021 restated 14.3455; FY2022 statutory 19.3381; FY2023 32.8947; FY2024 35.0207; FY2025 50.2330; FY2026 105.9169. Revenue is consistent across the old restated/statutory bridge, although PAT and CFO are not interchangeable. Five-year FY2021–26 CAGR is 49.16%, using six observations; three-year FY2023–26 is 47.67%. A comparable ten-year series was not established and is ND. Annual additions FY2022–26 were ₹4.9926/13.5566/2.1260/15.2123/55.6839 crore. Latest annual growth was 110.85%. [P1][H23][H24][H25][S1]

Assembly contributed ₹46.9451 crore, or 84.3%, of the latest revenue addition; engineering added ₹8.7388 crore. This is a disclosed expansion of the existing entity, not an acquired consolidated perimeter. It does not establish the exact unit/price/currency contribution. FY2026 H1 revenue was ₹41.3818 crore and H2 ₹64.5351 crore, versus prior H2 ₹31.1734 crore. H2 PAT ₹8.4521 crore compares with ₹3.9403 crore. No FY2027 half-year earnings are annualized from order updates. [RESULT][S1]

The preferred five-year schedule starts REV at9, but Medium confidence in underlying price/volume decomposition caps it at 8. The small base is not itself a penalty. National calendar2025 passenger growth of 4.80%, with December provisional, is contextual only: aircraft traffic and equipment procurement are not the same market, so the difference cannot be called a quantified share gain. [IND]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The base path assumes FY2027 sales ₹150 crore, approximately ₹80 crore assembly and ₹70 crore engineering/services/distribution, then annual sales ₹180/212.4/244.26/273.5712/300.92832 crore. This is an analyst execution case, not a relabeled management target. The July backlog of ₹141.19 crore includes ₹27.01 crore of whole-duration AMC contracts and ₹27.14 crore spares; it cannot all be scheduled as one-year revenue. The June-to-July backlog increase is not verified net bookings: the July update separately identifies only about ₹1.89 crore new orders. Pipeline and L1 positions are not awarded contracts. [JUNE][JULY]

Management discussed doubling physical capacity, initially through leased space, and ₹350–400 crore bidding capability. Neither is achieved revenue. The base funds ₹10 crore initial capex and then 5% of sales, broad WC at 47% of annual sales, and operating bank deposits at 9%. Terminal PPE is approximately ₹78.70 crore, compared with ₹27.29 crore March2026 PPE/CWIP. Assumed 17% operating EBIT is below FY2026 18.71%, recognizing the lower assembly margin. [CALL][S1]

Three-year incremental operating return is approximately 15.76% against an explicitly analytical 13–16% INR cost-of-capital range. The latest one-year proxy is higher, but combines commissioning and utilization of earlier investment; it is not a project IRR. Including operating deposits and CWIP prevents a misleading asset-light return. GQS raw 6.50 is capped at 5 because cumulative cash realization remains negative. Growth opportunities alone do not override this evidence.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter control is concentrated. The preferential notice’s proforma promoter-group holding is 3,882,080 shares, 51.69% after the June issue versus 62.06% before; this is the complete group, not only the two largest named holders. The actual allotment was to nonpromoters. Current encumbrance should be checked against the latest pattern before implementation; it is not inferred clear from an annual list. [EGM][ALLOT]

The reviewed FY2026 statutory/IFC opinions are unmodified. July’s board record recommends a second five-year term for Goyal Goyal & Co.; this is a reappointment, not an adverse auditor resignation. Shiny George’s July departure was as an independent director, not CFO. CFO transition and the subsequent professional CEO appointment warrant continuity monitoring, but no misconduct is inferred from personnel changes. [S1][GOV][CEO]

Commercial exposure deserves scrutiny: related vendor advances ₹4.1437 crore, related capex ₹2.6977 crore and director remuneration ₹1.2424 crore, about 9% of PAT. These balances are not automatically diversion; arm’s-length benchmarking and collection/delivery are the unresolved economic questions. Bank submissions showed Q1 receivables ₹24.6836 crore in books versus ₹20.0842 crore reported to the bank, explained as an omitted sale in the submission. Q4 book/bank stock difference ₹0.342 crore was attributed to direct-cost loading; receivables differed by minus₹0.5538 crore for TDS/deposit adjustments. Direction and explanation matter: these are not evidence that bank collateral was systematically overstated. [S1]

Promises versus delivery: March rating recorded a roughly ₹105 crore FY2026 revenue target, followed by audited ₹105.9169 crore; assembly scaling is achieved. May capacity doubling and bid-capability claims remain to be verified through qualified output and cash collections. October approved bonus/migration resolutions are not proof that either corporate action is operationally complete. [RATING][S1][CALL][VOTE]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
All figures below are ₹ crore except EPS, on the statutory standalone basis. Operating EBIT equals PBT plus finance cost minus all other income; EBITDA adds D&A. A comparable audited gross-profit line is ND because direct costs, goods and services are mixed. The structured history contains ratios, normalized PAT and balance-sheet detail. [S1][H25][H24][H23]

FY2022: revenue 19.3381; operating EBITDA 3.7001; EBIT 3.4992; PAT 2.1444; CFO -1.4630; cash capex 2.4878; FCF proxy -3.9508; debt 5.8094; equity 4.8834; reported diluted EPS ₹5.35.
FY2023: revenue 32.8947; operating EBITDA 7.2087; EBIT 7.0083; PAT 4.4383; CFO -9.2709; cash capex 0.3145; FCF proxy -9.5854; debt 2.8804; equity 25.2717; reported diluted EPS ₹9.84.
FY2024: revenue 35.0207; operating EBITDA 6.3140; EBIT 6.0957; PAT 4.5176; CFO 2.0511; cash capex 4.8742; FCF proxy -2.8231; debt 3.4826; equity 29.7893; reported diluted EPS ₹8.06.
FY2025: revenue 50.2330; operating EBITDA 9.6439; EBIT 9.0654; PAT 6.4901; CFO -16.7303; cash capex 10.7988; FCF proxy -27.5291; debt 7.9053; equity 58.8150; reported diluted EPS ₹10.56.
FY2026: revenue 105.9169; operating EBITDA 20.9326; EBIT 19.8174; PAT 13.8753; CFO 8.3248; cash capex 9.5457; FCF proxy -1.2209; debt 11.7778; equity 72.6903; reported diluted EPS ₹22.18.

FY2024–26 cumulative CFO is minus₹6.3544 crore against PAT ₹24.883 crore, conversion minus25.54%; five-year conversion is minus 54.31%. Three-year reported fixed-asset FCF proxy is minus₹31.5731 crore; five-year minus₹45.1093 crore. Cash capex is not the explanation for weak CFO. Receivables, unbilled work, vendor advances, inventory and operating deposits are the relevant bridge. Removing the net three-year deposit movement leaves CFO minus₹5.4806 crore; the deposits still need financing. Finance interest is outside reported CFO, making this proxy more generous than cash after financing. [S1][H25][H24][H23]

FY2026 closing trade receivables plus unbilled revenue were 44.75% of sales versus 46.53% a year earlier. Average trade-receivable days were about 94.5 using total revenue as a proxy, not including unbilled assets. Over-six-month receivables fell to ₹0.9695 crore, genuine contrary evidence to the poor cumulative conversion. Unbilled ageing is not independently supplied. Trade payables include₹2.5527 crore aged 2–3 years; collections should not be judged by cash supported by indefinitely delayed suppliers. [S1]

Broad operating WC ₹48.1349 crore includes ordinary statutory, expense and both current/noncurrent employee provisions. Opening tax ₹1.7704 crore and accrued interest ₹0.0014 crore are excluded and explicitly paid once. Recognized MSME interest is not added again. Of a ₹0.1063194 crore GST demand, accepted ₹0.045982 crore is already a liability; only the contested ₹0.0603374 crore is separately modeled as paid. This is a conservative settlement assumption, not a finding that the appeal fails. [S1]

Operating invested capital, including deposits and PPE/CWIP, is ₹24.4815/31.6148/66.5951/85.0222 crore for March 2023–26. At an assumed 25.5% operating tax rate, latest average-capital ROIC is 19.48% and the three-year incremental proxy 15.76%. Government-balance classification and recent capital commissioning limit precision; no unsupported five-year project return is supplied. The prospectus explicitly bridges FY2022 statutory PAT ₹2.1444 crore to restated₹2.4294 through gratuity, donation, tax/deferred-tax and prior-period adjustments. These series are not spliced silently. Later receivable/advance and expense/provision reclassifications leave total capital unchanged. [P1][H24][H25][S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹700 and current shares, trailing FY2026 P/E is approximately 37.9 times: current-share EPS ₹18.48 differs from historical weighted EPS ₹22.18. A March-only EV would mix stale cash with June-issued shares; the model instead bridges the actual financing and modeled intervening operations. [S1][ALLOT][M1]

The linked five-year outcomes are base ₹854.67 per share /4.07% annual return; bear ₹200.07/−22.16%; bull ₹1,772.39/20.42%; severe ₹72.49/−36.46%. Terminal multiples of operating NOPAT are 16/11/20/8 respectively. These are assumed ranges, not targets, guarantees or copied peer multiples. Base 15%-hurdle entry arithmetic is ₹424.92; changing the hurdle to 12% or 18% gives ₹484.96 or ₹373.58. The margin 14–20% versus multiple 12–20 grid produces a broad ₹252–633 entry range. None is an observable fair value.

Annual schedules fund capex, broad WC, collateral, income tax, disputed-claim sensitivity, issue costs, interest and debt maturities. Actual June ₹49.98784 crore cash is matched to 0.75098 crore current shares. The ₹41.6486 crore working-capital earmark is used for permitted operating outflows, not excluded and financed again; no inception dividend is assumed. Model gross purchases/running costs exceed that earmark, but actual utilization must be checked. Current/noncurrent employee obligations already in broad WC are not deducted twice. The funded asset model separates non-depreciable land from depreciable property; maintenance/growth spending is not zero, and a ₹10 crore extra-capex sensitivity is supplied. [EGM][ALLOT][S1]

Base 17% EBIT and 16-timesNOPAT require approximately 31.84% annual revenue growth after assumed FY2027 ₹150 crore to meet the 15% investor hurdle, ending near ₹597.53 crore annual revenue. The financed reverse case additionally requires about ₹43.69 crore hypothetical equity; it is not an approved raise. Base growth slows instead, ending near ₹300.93 crore. WC 60% reduces base IRR to 2.67%; extra ₹10 crore capex to 3.82%; ₹5 crore receivable impairment to 3.91%. Half the March deposits being free barely changes value because future collateral must still be funded. Investor taxes and actual trading impact are not included; implementation can reduce returns.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest challenge is that OEM-linked sales scale faster than retained cash or defensible per-share value. Airport tender delays or OEM loss can reduce utilization and margin while acceptance, unbilled work and vendor advances hold capital. The linked bear uses slow sales growth, 11% EBIT, 60% WC, 12% deposit requirement, a ₹3 crore asset impairment and 11-timesNOPAT; the severe case combines a sales contraction, 4–8% EBIT, 70% WC, 15% collateral and₹8 crore impairment. Impairment reduces the opening WC asset and is added back as a noncash charge before lost collection/replacement funding is calculated, so it is charged once.

Fresh equity allows the modeled business to survive these cases without additional rescue funding, yet the shareholder at ₹700 can suffer a 71% bear or 90% severe loss. That is high impairment risk driven by earning-power/valuation disappointment, not an asserted imminent default. A future inability to draw sanctioned facilities or a larger unverified cash deployment could worsen the path. The thesis-break variable is sustained failure to turn billed and unbilled revenue into cash while new capital keeps being required. A quoted price decline alone is not proof of business failure. [S1][BANK][ALLOT]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
At the dated₹700 price, 5× and 10× mean ₹3,500 and₹7,000 per current share before dividends. At an illustrative 20-times terminal P/E with no additional dilution, required PAT is about ₹131.42 crore or ₹262.84 crore, compared with FY2026₹13.8753 crore. At a 15% owner margin, revenue would need roughly ₹876 crore or ₹1,752 crore. These are reverse requirements, not supported forecasts. Actual funding would add WC, capex and possible dilution, raising the hurdle.

The base annual terminal revenue is ₹300.93 crore and even the bull is ₹431.68 crore. Those paths do not support a five-year 5× claim. A longer horizon may change the arithmetic, but current OEM rights, cash conversion and capacity evidence do not establish it. Classification: speculative / unsupported at this entry price, not a multibagger promise. [S1][ALLOT][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections: FY2026 CFO ₹8.3248 crore but three-year cumulative minus₹6.3544 crore. Review each half-year. Another material cash outflow during profitable growth warrants investigation; repeated capital raising without improved cumulative realization would break the self-funded-growth thesis.
2. Contract assets: March unbilled₹11.5079 crore and trade receivables₹35.8925 crore. Track acceptance and ageing, not just sales growth. Broad WC materially above the 60% bear assumption requires a new funding model.
3. Old creditors:₹2.5527 crore aged 2–3 years. Verify settlement or commercial explanation; unexplained roll-forward into older buckets weakens the cash-quality case.
4. Preferential funds: actual gross₹49.98784 crore, earmarked working capital ₹41.6486 crore, estimated expenses ₹3.3392 crore, March 2027 intended utilization. Reconcile certified deployment and deposits; a material unapproved change or unexplained loss requires a gate reassessment.
5. OEM rights and services: confirm renewal dates, customer acceptance and AMC retention. Loss of a key authorization without an economic replacement is a thesis break, not normal quarterly volatility.
6. Capacity: distinguish lease signing, installed capacity, qualified equipment and billed output against May’s doubling ambition. Delayed qualification should lower the revenue ramp and increase funding needs.
7. Funding: October cash limit ₹27.95 crore and nonfund ₹70.75 crore; factoring ₹15 crore has recourse. Monitor actual utilization, margin deposits and covenants, not summed headline facility numbers.
8. Governance/capital: benchmark related advances ₹4.1437 crore and related capex ₹2.6977 crore; reconcile subsequent liquidation/delivery. Verify bonus allotment and completed migration before adjusting shares or execution assumptions. This is a research monitoring plan, not an automated alert service. [S1][ALLOT][EGM][CALL][BANK][FACTOR][VOTE]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Weak setup / value-trap risk under the canonical matrix: BQS 5.70, GQS 5.00, IAS 3.375. This classification does not allege wrongdoing and does not deny the company’s strong sales expansion. It reflects mediocre cash quality and insufficient supported base return at the dated price, despite strengthened funding. Compounder criteria are not met. Action category is research watchlist / wait for verified cash improvement and a better price, not a buy or sell instruction.

A substantially lower price can improve IAS without changing BQS/GQS. Sustained conversion and attractive incremental returns after full funded expansion can improve business/growth quality. A critical financial-reliability problem, loss of core rights or unavailable essential finance would instead require a hold or failure assessment. Apply the actual intended position, taxes and executable market conditions before any personal implementation decision.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources include audited FY2023–26 reports and their earlier comparatives, the IPO prospectus, the FY2026 result image, actual June allotment, preferential objects, July backlog and October funding/voting disclosures. The source ledger provides exact URLs, document dates and inspected locations; evidence rows distinguish disclosed facts, calculations, management statements and analyst assumptions. [S1][H25][H24][H23][P1][RESULT][ALLOT][EGM][JULY][BANK][VOTE]

Calculations use ₹ crore, standalone scope, operating EBIT excluding all other income, cumulative CFO/PAT as a ratio of sums, and broad operating capital including relevant deposits and benefits. Statutory versus IPO-restated PAT is explicitly reconciled. A separate current-share EPS is used for valuation; an unallotted bonus is not economic dilution. The linked model keeps operating assets, funds, obligations and shares matched, with dated interim-stub assumptions and two-way sensitivities.

Open questions that would materially improve confidence: complete OEM contracts and renewal rights; current customer concentration and unbilled ageing; certified preferential deployment; separable unrestricted versus pledged bank deposits; capacity qualification and margins; actual post-March cash; and live execution depth. The record does not claim these facts are known. Source gaps are proportionately reflected in Medium confidence, Conditional gates and assumptions, rather than an invented all-clear or automatic misconduct finding.

gates.reason: Unmodified audit and disclosed financing/RPT record reviewed. Related vendor advances and related capex need commercial benchmarking; no substantiated diversion or minority abuse identified. Concentrated promoter control and repeat capital raises remain relevant.

Audited aggregate statements reconcile. Statutory versus IPO restated PAT and later presentation reclassifications are kept distinct. Bank-submission differences have disclosed scope/timing explanations; no unresolved contradiction that invalidates aggregate model inputs was found. Forecast collections and OEM renewal terms are uncertain, not audited facts.

The actual June equity raise and executed October cash facilities support modeled obligations without an assumed new rescue in core cases. Working-capital intensity, guarantee collateral and lender conditions remain material. Nonfund facilities are not cash and with-recourse factoring is not operating collection.

Sixty observed traded sessions, but 400-share lot equals ₹2.8 lakh at the dated close. Reference ₹5 lakh cannot be represented exactly in board lots; concentration and end of mandatory market making limit implementation. No live spread/depth is observed.

limitations: Complete OEM contract duration, renewal and exclusivity rights were not independently verified; presented issuer claims are not assumed permanent.

Latest customer-level concentration, unbilled ageing, September cash and preferential utilization were not available in the reviewed records. These are bounded through conditional scenarios, not asserted as current verified balances.
Some annual comparative categories were reclassified. Historical statutory PAT/CFO series is kept separate from IPO restated figures; five-year project-return estimates are not claimed.

next_steps: Reconcile the next preferential utilization statement and actual bank-deposit restrictions to the modeled cash bridge.
Track half-year collections, unbilled ageing and old-creditor clearance before treating growth as cash-generative.
Obtain OEM renewal terms and evidence of capacity qualification, not merely new bids.

score_note: BQS 5.70; GQS raw 6.50 capped at 5 because persistent CASH 3; IAS 3.375. All canonical factors scored with Medium confidence. No governance or funding-failure override.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audits and disclosed nonpromoter financing are positives. Related advance/capex exposure and concentrated control require benchmarking; neither is evidence of diversion. A clean opinion alone is not a stewardship premium.

MOAT.reason: OEM service relationships, equipment qualifications and lifecycle support are useful barriers. Rights have exceptions and unverified renewal terms; BEML and other specialist suppliers show contestability. This is not ownership of the global OEM technology.

REV.reason: Chosen five-year revenue CAGR 49.16% starts at 9 under the framework; Medium confidence in organic price/volume decomposition caps the historical factor at 8. Statutory segment expansion and both FY26 half-years support growth; no extra small-base penalty or TAM bonus.

DUR.reason: Growing installed equipment and service needs provide runway, with multiple OEM categories. Airport concentration, lumpy tender budgets and non-one-year backlog limit visibility; passenger traffic is not a guaranteed equipment order stream.

CAP.reason: Three-year incremental proxy 15.76% is around the upper end of an analytical 13–16% INR cost-of-capital range, not a proven project IRR. The latest high incremental result reflects commissioning/utilization and capital raised earlier; funding deposits and new WC cannot be omitted.

CASH.reason: Negative cumulative three- and five-year CFO despite substantial profits is a recurring weakness; deposit reclassification does not remove it. FY26 improvement and lower aged receivables are meaningful contrary evidence, but continued unbilled sales/advances and aged creditors prevent treating this as a resolved one-off.

BAL.reason: Actual fresh equity and executed working-capital facility materially improve resilience. Core modeled stresses need no additional rescue equity; current debt is modest relative to operating earnings. Future draw conditions, bank collateral and poor historical cash realization preclude a higher score.

EXEC.reason: FY26 sales exceeded the recorded ₹105 crore target and assembly revenue scaled. Capacity doubling remains a commitment rather than a completed proof point, and consistent cash conversion has not followed accounting growth.

EARN.reason: Operating EBIT growth, not large treasury gains, explains most profit improvement; current-share FY26 earnings remain above prior-year comparable earnings after dilution. Lower-margin assembly mix and working-capital-dependent earnings temper durability, with cash assessed separately.

R.reason: Supported base IRR 4.0734% is 10.9266 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, mapping exactly to R1; bull is not substituted for the base.

D.reason: Bear terminal ₹200.07 implies 71.4% loss and severe ₹72.49 nearly 89.6% loss. The raise supports business survival in these cases, but does not protect a shareholder paying ₹700 against lost earning power and multiple normalization.

P.reason: With FY27 revenue ₹150 crore and base 17% EBIT / 16 times NOPAT, subsequent annual growth approximately 31.84% is needed to meet the 15% investor hurdle after funding. Strong historical growth makes this possible, but it requires sustained execution beyond the decelerating base and leaves little margin for cash/margin error.

L.reason: Theoretical 2.37-day exit starts at L7. Explicit two-point downgrade to 5 reflects ₹2.8 lakh board lots, less-than-100-PAN caution and expired mandatory market making, alongside unobserved depth. Sixty actual trading days are not relabeled no-trade days; numeric exit is conditional, not a fill guarantee.

historical_audit.historical_reconciliation: Prospectus F11–12 explicitly reconciles FY22 statutory PAT2.1444 torestated2.4294: gratuity+.4008,donation+.0153,tax+.0058,deferred−.1787,prior+.0418cr. FY21stat.7558→rest.7351. Revenueunchanged. Keep annual statutory cash/PAT series separate from older restated CFO; FY22 restatedCFO−.3369 versus annual−1.463.

assumption_basis: The valuation is as of 20 October 2026, at the 19 October close of ₹700. Annual flows start from the audited March 2026 balance sheet, include the known June raise, and model the unknown intervening operating period rather than assert an October cash balance. The terminal date is 19 October 2031; the last FY32 stub is 202/365 of a year. Investor holding return spans five years.

Base FY27 revenue ₹150 crore can be decomposed into approximately ₹80 crore assembly and ₹70 crore engineering/services/distribution, versus audited FY26 ₹53.407 crore and ₹52.5099 crore. This requires additional execution and intake: July backlog ₹141.19 crore includes full multi-year service durations and is not one-year revenue. Subsequent annual base revenue is ₹180/212.4/244.26/273.5712/300.92832 crore, slowing rather than repeating the historical doubling.

Base operating EBIT margin is 17%, below FY26 18.71%. Manufacturing/assembly segment margin was approximately 15.14%, below engineering 24.33% before unallocated costs. A rising assembly share is not assumed to improve margins. Bear EBIT 11% and bull 20% are analyst scenarios, not management guidance. Other income, including treasury interest, is excluded.

The model keeps all ₹9.5964 crore March bank deposits as operating collateral because the report mixes term deposits and pledged balances without a separable free amount. Base required deposits are 9% of annual revenue; a half-release sensitivity changes opening available cash and then funds the same future collateral stock, so release is not double counted.

Broad operating working capital is ₹48.1349 crore. It includes unbilled revenue, retentions, vendor advances, operational deposits and all ordinary statutory, employee and expense liabilities, including both gratuity maturities. Future 47% base, 60% bear and 42% bull ratios are consistent broad closing stocks. Opening net tax ₹1.7704 crore and excluded accrued interest ₹0.0014 crore settle once in FY27. The contested GST ₹0.0603374 crore is conservatively paid once; accepted GST is already in statutory liabilities. Recognized MSME interest is not added a second time.

The actual ₹49.98784 crore June preferential raise is received once in FY27 against current issued shares of 0.75098 crore. Estimated issue costs ₹3.3392 crore are paid once. ₹41.6486 crore of proceeds is earmarked for working capital and ₹5 crore for general corporate purposes, with expected utilization by March 2027. These are available for authorized business outflows, not a dividend at inception. Modeled gross operating purchases and running costs exceed the working-capital earmark; no separate deployment deduction is added on top of modeled expenses, WC and capex. Actual utilization remains to be checked against the next statement.

Capex is ₹10 crore in the first base year, then 5% of annual revenue, with a proportionate terminal stub. Depreciation uses 4.5% of opening net depreciable assets plus a half-period charge on additions; ₹2.4386 crore leasehold land is excluded from depreciation. This is a blended analytical rate near the latest total charge, not a claim that the entire building or machinery estate requires five-year replacement. Sensitivity adds ₹10 crore capex. Cash rent stays within operating margins under Accounting Standards.

Debt costs 11%, with opening debt, half-year new borrowing and repayments solved together. Total modeled cash-debt ceiling is ₹27.95 crore, conservatively including vehicle borrowing within the disclosed fund-based envelope. ₹70.75 crore non-fund facilities are never counted as cash. The separate ₹15 crore with-recourse factoring limit is excluded from the reference and included only in a financing sensitivity, without treating financed receivables as improved operating collections.

Existing vehicle maturities are ₹0.1527 crore in FY27; the remaining ₹0.4135 crore is spread over four years as an explicit amortization estimate, tested within the available liquidity. Any unfinanced deficit would require hypothetical equity at a 30% discount to the dated price and 5% fees; none is required in the disclosed core cases. There are no forecast dividends, so retained cash is counted only at terminal.

Terminal multiples of operating NOPAT are 11/16/20 for bear/base/bull and 8 for severe. They are analyst ranges, not imported peer P/E ratios. Required operating deposits stay in the business and are not added to terminal equity. Available cash is added and debt deducted once. A future 2:5 bonus changes shares and price proportionately, not intrinsic business value; no unallotted bonus is applied to the current quote.

Forecast impairments reduce opening working-capital assets and reported PAT, are added back as noncash expense, and reduce the opening stock used to calculate required replacement working capital. Lost collection/replacement funding is therefore charged once, not as a fictional extra cash write-off. No income-tax benefit is assumed for the hypothetical write-off.
